title: Addition of RNA Sequins to Sample for RNA Sequencing
author: Tim Mercer
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.x8cfrsw

steps.title: Store sequins at -80 °C
steps.instruction: Upon receipt, verify that the RNA sequins have not thawed during shipment and immediately transfer them to frozen storage at –80 °C; do not store them in a –20 °C frost‑free freezer.

steps.title: Prepare single‑use aliquots
steps.instruction: On first thaw, spin the tube containing 10 µL of RNA sequins (15 ng/µL) to collect the liquid at the tube bottom, then aliquot the required amount for a single use based on the sample input amount recommended in Table 1 and the chosen mixture (A or B).

steps.title: Dilute aliquoted sequins
steps.instruction: Dilute the aliquoted RNA sequins to the concentration specified in Table 1 (or to an absolute amount if using the absolute‑addition approach) using nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Add sequins to sample RNA
steps.instruction: Add the diluted RNA sequins directly to the sample RNA before any downstream processing such as poly‑A enrichment or rRNA depletion. Use Mix A for one experimental condition and Mix B for the other; do not add both mixtures to the same sample.

steps.title: Concentrate RNA if required
steps.instruction: If the downstream library‑preparation workflow requires a higher RNA concentration after sequin addition, concentrate the combined RNA using one of the following methods: ethanol precipitation, SPRI® bead purification (e.g., RNAClean® XP), column‑based cleanup (e.g., RNA Clean & Concentrator™ Kit), or vacuum centrifugation.

steps.title: Prepare library and sequence
steps.instruction: Proceed with library preparation according to the protocol of your chosen library‑preparation kit, then sequence the library per the manufacturer’s instructions (e.g., on an Illumina HiSeq 2500).
